findings.title: Every tool card shows the same wrench glyph in place of a thumbnail
findings.description: All ten cards on the find page carry an identical pale-green tile with a wrench, whether the tool is a ladder, pressure washer or wallpaper steamer. DESIGN.md lists 'a thumbnail' as part of the card, so this reads as a placeholder left on show.
findings.impact: The largest visual element on each card carries no information, so members comparing the two-battery and one-battery drills, or scanning for a ladder, get no visual cue; it is also the main reason the page may read as unfinished.
findings.recommendation: Decide what each card image is for: the actual library item, or a mark specific to each category; if neither exists yet, remove the tile rather than show a stand-in.

findings.title: No identity beyond the name in bold text and no focal point on any surface
findings.description: The brand is a stock wrench glyph beside 'Fernhill Tool Library' in the body face. Ground, type and colour are the category default for a community service; nothing from the library's world (the room, the stock, the membership card, the desk) appears visually on any screen.
findings.impact: 'Neighbourly' is carried only by the copy; a first-time member may not tell this from any other booking form, and the design fails the swap, category-guess and similar-prompt tests.

evidence.detail: done page, nothing marks the moment

findings.recommendation: Decide an identity floor drawn from the library itself (the referent the green came from, the stock, the desk) and carry it through the name and one recurring element; Operate mode allows identity without hero moments.

findings.title: Tool names truncate to identical strings on phones
findings.description: At 375 card titles are cut with an ellipsis; both drills read 'Cordless drill 18 V, co...', and other titles lose the distinguishing spec ('Extension ladder 3 m ...', 'Pressure washer, 130 ...').
findings.impact: Phones are the main device; the distinguishing words ('two batteries' vs 'one battery') are what members use to pick a tool, and they are hidden.
findings.recommendation: Decide whether titles wrap at narrow widths, or which part of the name must always stay visible.

findings.title: Sticky Reserve bar covers the pick-up calendar, including the chosen day
findings.description: In the captures at 1280 and 375 the white action bar sits across the calendar's second week; the selected day (Mon 12 or Sat 17) is hidden under it, and the 'Added to your basket' toast sits over the weekday header.
findings.impact: The calendar is the task on this page; the primary button competes with and occludes it, so members may not see which day they picked before reserving. Behaviour while scrolling cannot be confirmed from stills.
findings.recommendation: Decide where the reserve action sits relative to the calendar so the chosen day stays visible, and check it in the scrolling viewport.

findings.title: Basket session cards break into one full-width row and five cramped cards at 1280
findings.description: Six session radios render as one full-width card (Wednesday 28 October) then five narrow cards whose labels wrap to three lines.
findings.impact: The layout implies the first session is special and makes the others harder to read, on the step where the member chooses when to turn up.
findings.recommendation: Decide one layout for the session list at wide widths in which every option has equal weight and readable labels.

findings.title: Filter panel uses unthemed browser-default date and select controls
findings.description: 'Available from' is a native yyyy/mm/dd date input with the browser calendar icon, and Category is a native select with a different border and chevron from the styled Loan length select.
findings.impact: The yyyy/mm/dd mask contradicts the declared 'Saturday 17 October' format, and the mismatch signals unfinish in the one place members check what can be collected on a day.
findings.recommendation: Decide whether filters follow the same control styling as the tool page and the declared date format.

findings.title: Basket and done pages end with an empty grey band under the footer
findings.description: At 1280 the footer stops mid-viewport and the page ground continues below it.
findings.impact: A visible sign of unfinish on the confirmation moment; low cost but present on every short page.
findings.recommendation: Decide how short pages fill the viewport.

findings.title: Masthead still says 'Basket (1)' after the reservation is confirmed
findings.description: On the done page the navigation shows Basket (1), as if the drill were still held.
findings.impact: Members may wonder whether the reservation went through or whether the tool is still waiting in the basket.
findings.recommendation: Decide what the basket count shows once a reservation is made.

findings.title: Details list splits into two misaligned columns
findings.description: Category, Deposit and Available from align values at about x=224; Chuck, Batteries, Weight and Case align at about x=180, with a different row gap.
findings.impact: Small, but it undercuts 'careful': the one specification table looks assembled from two parts.
findings.recommendation: Decide whether specs and loan facts are one list or two clearly separate ones.

_strengths: Copy in the desk volunteer's voice, concrete and in members' words ('Enough for a day of fixing shelves and a fence', 'We text you if a tool is returned late by the previous borrower').
Dark theme composed rather than inverted: lighter cards on a dark green-grey, mint accent.
One filled button per page; deposit shown on every tool; clear error summary on basket.
_keep: Keep the concrete volunteer voice and the one-filled-button discipline; add identity, not more buttons or chrome.
_not_assessable: whether the green matches the physical membership card
